newsitem.title: USA: Clint Eastwood takes stand in civil trial.
newsitem.headline: Clint Eastwood takes stand in civil trial.

text.p: Clint Eastwood took the stand in court on Monday in a civil case filed against him by a former lover who alleges he sabotaged her screen career after they broke up.

Speaking in a monotone, the actor who came to fame as a man of few words in a series of 1960's westerns answered just "yes" or "no" to about a dozen questions from Sondra Locke's lawyer, who rested her case after five minutes.

During questioning Eastwood said he had signed an indemnity contract with Warner Bros. Pictures agreeing to pay almost $1.5 million to cover the studio for losses it might incur from a contract it had with Locke to direct films.
The Academy Award-winning director told Locke's attorney, Peggy Garrity, that he knew Locke had no knowledge of his deal with Warner Bros.

Locke, an actress who lived with Eastwood for 13 years after they met on the set of the 1975 movie "The Outlaw Josey Wales," alleges in her suit that Eastwood's deal to pay Warner Bros. essentially destroyed her directorial career in Hollywood.
"I felt annoyed, I felt embarrassed, I felt humiliated," Locke told the jurors last week when she testified.

Her directorial efforts, "Ratboy" in 1986 and "Impulse" in 1989, were not commercial successes and in three years under the Warner Bros. contract, none of her 30 suggested projects was ever developed into a film.
The case stems from Locke's original 1989 palimony lawsuit against Eastwood in which she claimed assets the couple accumulated during their relationship.

Locke later dropped the palimony suit when Eastwood agreed to secure the director's contract worth $1.5 million at Warner Bros. for her. But Locke now claims she was defrauded and is seeking damages of over $2.5 million.
Eastwood's lawyer Raymond Fisher has said the actor-director had no intent to defraud Locke and only made the deal with Warner Bros. to help her directorial career.
